messages.text:
In the same spirit, if no inner solenoid is present, the detector enevelopos can be reshuffled to fill the space accordingly

Let the sytem engineer talk to the sub system engineers to make sure the new allocations still meet their requirements.

I’ll have the system architect coordinate with the tracker and calorimeter engineers on reallocating the former inner-solenoid space, then check the muon interfaces. We’ll document the tradeoffs and redraw the affected candidates.

The tracker and calorimeter engineers recommend keeping the tracker and its service reserve, moving the ECal inward by 0.40 m, and giving that space to the HCal. The ECal endcap’s outer radius must also move inward to avoid overlapping the enlarged HCal barrel. Preliminary straight-ray checks show no reduced ECal or HCal envelope path length in the sampled directions; shower containment still needs simulation.

The muon engineer also supports the proposal conditionally: the HCal outer boundary, outer coil and stepped muon envelopes remain compatible. The revised layouts pass the overlap checks and a 5,201-direction ray comparison. I’m recording the agreement and alternatives in DES-004; material, segmentation, service capacity and field effects remain open validation tasks.

Updated [PR #6](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/6) after coordination between the system architect and tracker, calorimeter and muon engineers.

For **MAG-03/04/06**:

- ECal moves inward by **0.40 m**, preserving its thickness.
- HCal gains **0.40 m of radial assembly space**.
- Tracker/services, outer coil and stepped muon envelopes retain their allocations.

DES-004 now records the requirements, alternatives and revised drawings. **32 tests and CI passed**; 5,201 sampled directions showed no reduced ECal/HCal envelope path length.

Geometric constraints are preserved. Material, shower containment, segmentation and service capacity remain subject to validation and human review.
